A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 22-page versions of the same work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A–D, and final LVIS category list support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original retrieval experiments on HierOpenImages and LVIS, VOC/COCO evaluations, cross-image ablations, and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains and revises these original experiments and adds a comparison of retrieval metrics in Appendix Table 5.

M1.justification: v4 introduces two-stage retrieval that filters candidates by entailment angle and ranks the retained candidates by cosine similarity, replacing angle-only ranking in the principal tables. Equation 8 also changes the stated objective to aggregate all positives against all candidates. Multi-positive learning was already intended in v3, but the formulas are not equivalent.

E1.justification: Both versions use HierOpenImages/OpenImages for same-class and hierarchical retrieval, LVIS for generalization, and VOC/COCO for evaluation using ground-truth boxes. The represented datasets and tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 add fine-tuned HCL† evaluated with cosine similarity alongside the retained HCL and HCL† distance-based comparisons. The underlying CLIP, MoCo-v2, and HCL comparator families remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The principal retrieval comparisons switch from angle-only to gated cosine ranking. v4 also reports correcting an extra normalization issue affecting all methods. Appendix B.1 changes the stated effective batch sizes from 320 to 640 for CLIP and from 800 to 1984 for MoCo-v2; these are reported setting revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 5 systematically compares cosine similarity, entailment angle, and gated retrieval across both encoders and retrieval directions, adding a substantive analysis of the ranking components. Existing cross-image ablations are revised and retained as Tables 6–7. Figures 6 and 10 remove the Gaussian-blur sigma=20 condition while retaining sigma=5, sigma=10, and tiny-crop analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The empirical distribution plots do not introduce a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Values throughout Tables 1–4 and the cross-image ablations are extensively revised, with additional results in new Table 5. For example, CLIP's child-to-parent Top-5 score changes from 26.73 to 53.04 in Table 1. LVIS OT rankings change from hyperbolic ties or wins to Euclidean wins at all three cutoffs in Table 3. Changed normalization, training settings, and retrieval rules prevent interpreting these replacements as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Equation 8 substantively revises the loss definition from a per-pair positive term normalized against that positive and negatives to summed positives normalized against all candidates. The remaining hyperbolic definitions, entailment relations, and Wasserstein formulation are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about learning user-defined visual hierarchies without explicit hierarchical labels, contrastive entailment learning, hierarchical evaluation, and generalization.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the no-cross-image ablation as evidence that hyperbolic geometry implicitly learns visually dissimilar hierarchical relationships. v4 removes that inference and discusses semantic-alignment benefits with a precision cost from cross-image variability. Appendix B.2 adds a substantive mechanism and qualification: fine-tuning changes coarse hierarchical organization while strong pretrained similarity relationships persist, motivating gated cosine ranking.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 supplies gating thresholds: 2 radians for MoCo and 2.5 for CLIP in small-k retrieval, and 1 for both in large-k retrieval. v4 updates batch-size disclosures and acknowledges the normalization issue, but removes the single-epoch budget and the approximately 26-hour CLIP and 18-hour MoCo training times.

R1.justification: The same 43 cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Reference differences concern citation page pointers rather than added or removed research.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the loss, revise experimental interpretations, expand Appendix B.2, and shorten Appendix C. The overall section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds metric-comparison Table 5, expands Tables 1–2, redraws the PR and embedding-distribution plots, and removes Figure 4's threshold annotations. Figure 7 is resized, Figure 10 moves, and the existing ablation tables become Tables 6–7. These are targeted display changes within the retained document layout.

improvement.justification: v4 reports correcting a normalization error affecting all methods (Section 5, footnote 4), addressing a serious defect in v3's central comparative evidence. Substantially revised baseline scores and the withdrawal of the strong no-cross-image superiority interpretation make the empirical account more credible. New Table 5 also exposes the contributions of different retrieval rules. Removing epoch counts and training times weakens reproducibility, but this limited loss is outweighed by correcting the central results and their interpretation.
